История КПСС — History of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union
Full bibliographic citation — История Коммунистической партии Советского Союза (History of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union). Издание шестое, дополненное (6th supplemented edition). Подготовлено авторским коллективом (authorial collective): Б. Н. Пономарев, академик (руководитель / head of the collective); М. С. Волин, доктор исторических наук; В. С. Зайцев, доктор исторических наук; И. И. Минц, академик; А. Д. Педосов, доктор исторических наук; В. И. Попов, доктор исторических наук; А. И. Соболев, доктор философских наук; К. И. Суворов, доктор исторических наук; Б. С. Тельпуховский, доктор исторических наук. — Москва: Политиздат (Издательство политической литературы), 1982. — 784 с. The fundamentals of chapters X, XI, XV and XVII rest on materials by И. М. Волков, А. П. Кучкин, Л. А. Слепов, А. А. Тимофеевский and академик В. М. Хвостов. Заведующий редакцией К. К. Яцкевич; редакторы С. Н. Иванов, А. В. Качиурина, В. П. Шальнева. Сдано в набор 06.08.81; подписано в печать 18.11.81; тираж 400 000 (1—150 000) экз.





































WorkThe official party history textbook — a single-volume narrative of the history of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union from the origins of Russian Marxism to the XXVI Party CongressEditionИздание шестое, дополненное (6th supplemented edition), Политиздат, Москва, 1982; 784 pp.; print run 400,000 (first 150,000)Editorial leadershipAuthorial collective headed by академик Б. Н. Пономарев; chapter fundamentals drawn from И. М. Волков, А. П. Кучкин, Л. А. Слепов, А. А. Тимофеевский, В. М. ХвостовStructurePreface (Предисловие), twenty chapters (Главы I–XX) each with dated period band and numbered sections, chapter conclusions (Краткие выводы), and a closing Заключение (Conclusion); table of contents at the end of the volumePeriod1883 (Plekhanov’s «Освобождение труда» / Liberation of Labour group) through the XXVI Congress of the CPSU (23 February – 3 March 1981), with planning horizons to 1985/1990 — i.e. 1883 to early 1981Coverage in this wiki’s spanChapters XVI–XX (1945–1981): postwar reconstruction, the world socialist system, developed socialism, and the Congresses from XIX to XXVI — the Cold-War-era history of the CPSUOCR noteArchive.org scan OCR; the Roman numerals in chapter headings garble heavily (П/У/УГ/Х!/ЖУ/Хх! etc. for II/III/VI/XI/XIV/XVII), and section-page numbers interleave as noise. Clean chapter titles are reconstructed from the end-of-volume table of contents (оглавление) paired with body openers
Structure and contents
Chapter headings below are the reconstructed clean titles (English translation + original). Section sub-headings are given from the volume’s table of contents.
Глава I. Начало рабочего движения и распространение марксизма в России (1883–1894 годы)
The beginning of the workers’ movement and the spread of Marxism in Russia. Sections: development of capitalism and the position of the masses in the second half of the XIX century; the revolutionary-democratic movement and the first workers’ organisations; Plekhanov and the «Освобождение труда» (Liberation of Labour) group, Marxist circles in Russia, the beginning of V. I. Lenin’s revolutionary activity.
Глава II. Борьба за создание марксистской партии в России. Образование РСДРП. Возникновение большевизма (1894–1904 годы)
The struggle to create a Marxist party in Russia; the formation of the RSDLP; the emergence of Bolshevism. Sections: the beginning of the Leninist stage in the development of Marxism; Lenin’s struggle against populism and «legal Marxism»; the Petersburg «Союз борьбы за освобождение рабочего класса»; the I Congress of the RSDLP; the Leninist plan for building the party and the fight of «Искра»; the II Congress of the RSDLP and the emergence of the party of Bolsheviks; the struggle against the Mensheviks.
Глава III. Партия большевиков в революции 1905–1907 годов
The Bolshevik party in the revolution of 1905–1907. Sections: the revolutionary movement on the eve of 1905, the Russo-Japanese war, the Ninth of January, the start of the first Russian revolution; the Bolshevik assessment of the character, forces and tasks of the revolution; the III Congress; the rise of the revolution, the All-Russian political strike, the formation of the Soviets, the December armed uprising; party building in conditions of revolution; the IV and V Congresses, Duma tactics and the defeat of the revolution; the international significance of the revolution.
Глава IV. Партия большевиков в период реакции (1907–1910 годы)
The Bolshevik party in the period of reaction. Sections: the Stolypin reaction; the Bolshevik struggle for the party against the liquidators, otsovists and Trotskyists; Lenin’s defence and development of the philosophy of Marxism and of the doctrine of the party; the party’s struggle to win the working masses and prepare a new revolution.
Глава V. Партия большевиков в годы нового революционного подъема (1910–1914 годы)
The Bolshevik party in the years of the new revolutionary upsurge. Sections: the collapse of the Stolypin policy and the beginning of mass revolutionary actions; the Prague party conference; the Bolshevik newspaper «Правда»; the Bolshevik faction in the IV State Duma; the party at the head of the revolutionary struggle.
Глава VI. Партия большевиков в годы мировой империалистической войны. Вторая революция в России (1914 год — февраль 1917 года)
The Bolshevik party in the years of the world imperialist war; the second revolution in Russia. Sections: the origins and causes of the First World War, the collapse of the II International; revolutionary work among the masses during the imperialist war; Lenin’s development of the theory of the socialist revolution; the February bourgeois-democratic revolution, the formation of Soviets of workers’ and soldiers’ deputies, dual power.
Глава VII. Партия — вдохновитель и организатор победы Великой Октябрьской социалистической революции (март — октябрь 1917 года)
The party as inspirer and organiser of the victory of the Great October Socialist Revolution. Sections: the domestic and international situation after the overthrow of tsarism, the party’s emergence from underground; Lenin’s April Theses, the VII (April) All-Russian conference, the course toward the transition of the bourgeois-democratic revolution into a socialist one; the struggle for the masses during dual power, the July days; the VI Congress, the course toward armed uprising, the defeat of the Kornilov mutiny; the preparation of the uprising and the victory of the October revolution; the causes and international significance of the victory.
Глава VIII. Борьба партии за развитие социалистической революции и упрочение Советской власти (октябрь 1917 года — 1918 год)
The party’s struggle to develop the socialist revolution and consolidate Soviet power. Sections: the party in the struggle to create the Soviet state, the first socialist transformations; the struggle to exit the war, the Treaty of Brest, the VII Congress of the RCP(b); the Leninist plan for building the foundations of a socialist economy, the first Soviet Constitution.
Глава IX. Партия в период иностранной военной интервенции и гражданской войны (1918–1920 годы)
The party in the period of foreign military intervention and civil war. Sections: the beginning of intervention and civil war, the party’s organisation of resistance; the collapse of German intervention, the intensification of Entente intervention; the formation of the III Communist International, the VIII Congress, the Second Party Programme; the turning point, the defeat of Kolchak and Denikin; the IX Congress, the defeat of Pilsudski’s and Wrangel’s forces, the end of intervention and civil war; the causes of the victory of Soviet power and the lessons of the civil war.
Глава X. Партия в борьбе за восстановление народного хозяйства. Образование Союза Советских Социалистических Республик (1921–1925 годы)
The party’s struggle for the restoration of the national economy; the formation of the USSR. Sections: the international and domestic situation after the civil war, the trade-union discussion; the X Congress and the transition to the New Economic Policy (NEP); the first successes of NEP, the XI Congress, the foreign policy of the Soviet state, the formation of the USSR; Lenin’s last articles and letters, the further development of the theory of revolution, of the plan for building socialism and of the doctrine of the party; the XII and XIII Congresses, the struggle against Trotskyism, the death of Lenin, the Leninist levy into the party; the course toward socialist industrialisation and the XIV Congress.
Глава XI. Борьба партии за социалистическую индустриализацию страны и подготовку сплошной коллективизации сельского хозяйства (1926–1929 годы)
The party’s struggle for socialist industrialisation and the preparation of wholesale collectivisation of agriculture. Sections: the international situation and foreign policy in 1926–1929; socialist industrialisation, the struggle against the Trotskyist-Zinovievite anti-party bloc; mobilising the people for industrialisation; the first successes, the XV Congress and the course toward collectivisation; the preparation of the socialist offensive across the whole front, the struggle against the right deviation, the adoption of the first five-year plan, the beginning of the mass kolkhoz movement.
Глава XII. Партия в период наступления социализма по всему фронту. Создание колхозного строя (1929–1932 годы)
The party in the period of the offensive of socialism across the whole front; the creation of the kolkhoz order. Sections: the economic crisis in the capitalist world and the international position of the USSR; the unfolding of wholesale collectivisation, the transition to the policy of liquidating the kulaks as a class, the XVI Congress; organisational and political work during the offensive; the struggle for the technical rearmament of the economy, the growth of the kolkhoz movement, the results of the first five-year plan.
Глава XIII. Борьба партии за завершение социалистической реконструкции народного хозяйства. Победа социализма в СССР (1933–1937 годы)
The party’s struggle for the completion of the socialist reconstruction of the national economy; the victory of socialism in the USSR. Sections: the beginning of fascist aggression and Soviet foreign policy amid the mounting war danger; the struggle to strengthen the socialist economy, the XVII Congress; the struggle for the early fulfilment of the second five-year plan, the victory of socialism in the USSR, the Soviet Constitution of 1936.
Глава XIV. Партия в борьбе за упрочение социалистического общества, усиление обороны страны (1937 год — июнь 1941 года)
The party in the struggle to consolidate socialist society and strengthen the country’s defence. Sections: the USSR’s struggle for peace and the security of peoples amid fascist aggression in 1937–1938; political work in conditions of socialism, the XVIII Congress; the struggle for collective resistance to fascist aggression in 1939, the beginning of the Second World War; organisational work in industry and the strengthening of industrial and defence capacity; the struggle to consolidate the kolkhoz order; the rise in the material and cultural level of life, the growth of the party’s ranks.
Глава XV. Партия в период Великой Отечественной войны (июнь 1941 года — 1945 год)
The party in the period of the Great Patriotic War. Sections: the treacherous German attack on the Soviet Union and the mobilisation of all forces; the Communist Party as organiser of the radical turning point in the war; the victorious completion of the war; the world-historical significance and sources of the Soviet victory.
Глава XVI. Борьба партии за восстановление и развитие социалистического народного хозяйства. Образование мировой системы социализма (1945–1952 годы)
The party’s struggle for the restoration and development of the socialist national economy; the formation of the world socialist system. Sections: fundamental changes in the international situation after the Second World War; the work of restoration and development, the early fulfilment of the fourth five-year plan; organisational and ideological work, the XIX Congress of the CPSU; the CPSU’s role in strengthening the community of socialist countries, the formation of the world socialist system.
Глава XVII. Партия в борьбе за развитие социалистического общества в СССР и упрочение мировой системы социализма (1952–1961 годы)
The party in the struggle for the development of socialist society in the USSR and the consolidation of the world socialist system. Sections: the struggle for peace against the aggressive policy of imperialism; cooperation with the socialist countries; the accelerated disintegration of the colonial system; the fifth five-year plan and the restoration of Leninist norms of party and state life; the XX Congress; the activity of the party to raise the role of state and public organisations, the XXI Congress, the full and final victory of socialism; the CPSU’s contribution to the cohesion of the international communist movement; the XXII Congress and the Third Party Programme.
Глава XVIII. Возрастание руководящей роли партии в период развитого социализма. Сплочение стран социалистического содружества (1962–1970 годы)
The growth of the party’s leading role in the period of developed socialism; the drawing together of the countries of the socialist community. Sections: the foreign-policy activity of the CPSU and the Soviet state, the consolidation of the socialist community; the struggle for the seven-year plan, the October 1964 Plenum of the CC and the restoration of Leninist norms; economic development 1965–1970; organisational and ideological work, the centenary of Lenin’s birth; the struggle of the CPSU and fraternal parties for the unity of the international communist movement; the XXIV Congress.
Глава XIX. Деятельность КПСС в условиях развитого социалистического общества. Успехи стран социалистического содружества (1971–1980 годы)
The activity of the CPSU in conditions of developed socialist society; the successes of the countries of the socialist community. Sections: the struggle to strengthen the positions of socialism and implement the Programme of Peace; the fiftieth anniversary of the USSR; the XXV Congress; the foreign-policy activity of the CPSU and the Soviet state; the struggle to raise the efficiency of production and perfect the economic mechanism; the further strengthening of the party and the raising of the level of its organisational and ideological-political work; the Constitution of developed socialism and the sixtieth anniversary of October; the Conference of Communist and Workers’ Parties of Europe.
Глава XX. XXVI съезд КПСС — съезд коммунистического созидания и мира
The XXVI Congress of the CPSU — a congress of communist construction and peace. Sections: in an atmosphere of unity, cohesion and efficiency; the international policy of the CPSU; the economic and social policy of the CPSU in the period of developed socialism; the tasks of the party in the socio-political and spiritual development of Soviet society; the party as vanguard of the Soviet people.
Заключение (Conclusion)
The volume closes with a concluding section (Заключение) on p. 758, drawing together the party’s historical path as presented in the twenty chapters.

История СССР, Том XI — History of the USSR, Volume 11: The Soviet Union on the Path to Developed Socialism (1945–1961)
Full bibliographic citation — История СССР с древнейших времен до наших дней (History of the USSR from Ancient Times to the Present Day), in twelve volumes. Вторая серия (Second series), Том XI (Volume 11): Советский Союз на пути к развитому социализму. 1945–1961 гг. (The Soviet Union on the Path to Developed Socialism, 1945–1961). Редакционная коллегия тома (volume editorial board): И. Б. Берхин (ответственный редактор / responsible editor), Р. Х. Аминова, М. А. Вылцан, А. В. Митрофанова, В. Е. Полетаев, С. С. Хесин (заместитель ответственного редактора / deputy responsible editor). — Москва: Издательство «Наука», 1980. — ~653 с. Ким (заместитель главного редактора) and others.

Structure and contents
Chapter headings below are the reconstructed clean titles (English translation + original). Section sub-headings are given from the volume’s table of contents.
Введение (Introduction)
Introduction. The changed international position of the Soviet Union after the Second World War: the victory in the Great Patriotic War, the USSR as a founding member of the United Nations, the formation of the world socialist system and the deepening of the general crisis of capitalism.
Часть первая — СССР в период восстановления и дальнейшего развития народного хозяйства. 1945–1950 гг.
Part One — The USSR in the period of restoration and further development of the national economy, 1945–1950.
Глава 1. Международное положение и внешняя политика СССР
The international position and foreign policy of the USSR. Sections: the formation of the world socialist system and the change in the correlation of forces between socialism and capitalism; the unfolding of the “cold war” against the Soviet Union and the people’s-democratic states; the Soviet Union’s struggle for peace and the security of peoples — the preparation and conclusion of democratic peace treaties with the former allies of Germany, the Soviet Union and the German question, the USSR in the United Nations; the USSR and the countries of people’s democracy — the establishment of a new type of international relations, Soviet aid to the people’s-democratic countries; the Soviet people at the head of the world movement of partisans of peace.
Глава 2. Переход Советской страны к мирному строительству
The transition of the Soviet country to peaceful construction. Sections: the Soviet Union after the Great Patriotic War — the main tasks of peaceful construction, territory, population, the state of the economy; the reconstruction of the life of the country on a peaceful footing — demobilisation of the army, repatriation of Soviet citizens, reconstruction of state and party organisations, the transition from a war to a peace economy, measures to improve the life and way of life of the people; the elaboration of the fourth five-year plan, elections to the Supreme Soviet of the USSR, the first session of the Supreme Soviet of the second convocation, the beginning of the all-people’s movement for the fulfilment of the five-year plan.
Глава 3. Политическая система социалистического общества во второй половине 40-х годов
The political system of socialist society in the second half of the 1940s. Sections: the enhancement of the leading role of the Communist Party — the growth of party ranks, the activity of party organisations, the strengthening of the ideological work of the party; the Soviets in the years of the fourth five-year plan — the activity of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR and the Supreme Soviets of the union republics, the local Soviets in the second half of the 1940s, the improvement of the organs of state administration, the postwar reorganisation and further strengthening of the Soviet Armed Forces; the trade unions and the Komsomol.
Глава 4. Восстановление и дальнейшее развитие промышленности и транспорта в годы четвертой пятилетки
The restoration and further development of industry and transport in the years of the fourth five-year plan. Sections: ensuring the conditions for the fulfilment of the plan in industry; the revival of industry in the territory that had been under occupation — the restoration of the damaged industrial centres of the Russian Federation, the revival of the industry of Ukraine and Belorussia, the results of the restoration; the further development of industry and transport — the strengthening of the fuel-energy and metallurgical base, the rise of machine-building, the growth of the production of consumer goods, the development of transport and communications; industrial cadres and the labour enthusiasm of workers in industry and transport; the results of the fourth five-year plan in industry and transport.
Глава 5. Борьба за восстановление и дальнейшее развитие сельского хозяйства
The struggle for the restoration and further development of agriculture. Sections: measures for the further strengthening of the kolkhoz order and the raising of agriculture — the tasks of the fourth five-year plan in agriculture, the February (1947) Plenum of the CC of the VKP(b); the growth of the productive forces of agriculture and the enlargement of the kolkhozes — the labour resources of the village, the strengthening of the material-technical base of agriculture, the training of qualified cadres, the enlargement of the kolkhozes; the achievement of the prewar level of agricultural production — the labour upsurge in the village, the development of agricultural production in the fourth five-year plan.
Глава 6. Повышение жизненного уровня советского народа в годы четвертой пятилетки
The raising of the standard of living of the Soviet people in the years of the fourth five-year plan. Sections: the material position and way of life of the population — the influence of the war on the level of life, the abolition of the rationing system, the growth of popular consumption, the currency reform, the increase of the real incomes of the working people, the restoration and improvement of towns and villages; concern for the health of Soviet people — the liquidation of the consequences of the war in public health, sanitary and medical service of the population, the development of physical culture and sport.
Глава 7. Культурное строительство в четвертой пятилетке
Cultural construction in the fourth five-year plan. Sections: cultural-mass work, public education, the training of specialists — the main tasks and features of cultural construction after the war, the restoration and extension of the network of cultural institutions and the means of mass propaganda, public education, the training of specialists; Soviet science — the main tasks of science in conditions of peaceful construction, the strengthening of the link of science with production, research in the natural sciences, the social sciences; literature and art — the main features of postwar development, literary life, Soviet art.
Глава 8. Построение социализма в молодых советских республиках и областях
The building of socialism in the young Soviet republics and regions. Sections: the development of the political system — party and state construction, the liquidation of bourgeois-nationalist bands; socialist industrialisation — the industrial development of the republics of the Baltic, the industrialisation of the Moldavian SSR, the western regions of the Ukrainian SSR and the Belorussian SSR, and the new regions of the RSFSR; the socialist transformation of agriculture — the agrarian reform in the Baltic republics, the preparation of mass collectivisation, the unfolding of mass collectivisation and the victory of the kolkhoz order in the Baltic republics, the victory of the kolkhoz order in the western regions of the Ukraine and Belorussia and in Right-Bank Moldavia; cultural construction — public education, the development of science, literature and art, the rise of cultural-educational work.
Часть вторая — Развитие социалистического общества в 50-х годах
Part Two — The development of socialist society in the 1950s.
Глава 9. Внешняя политика СССР в 50-х годах
The foreign policy of the USSR in the 1950s. Sections: the strengthening of the world socialist system — political cooperation of the socialist countries, resistance to imperialist aggression against the Korean People’s Democratic Republic and the Democratic Republic of Vietnam, the expansion of economic cooperation of the socialist countries; Soviet support for the national-liberation struggle of the peoples — the USSR and the Arab countries, assistance to the development of the young states of Asia and Africa; the struggle of the USSR for the easing of international tension and for peaceful coexistence with the capitalist countries — the growth of international tension at the beginning of the 1950s, Soviet proposals on the German question, Soviet efforts to create collective security in Europe, new Soviet proposals on disarmament, measures for the normalisation and improvement of relations with the capitalist countries, support of the peaceful position of the USSR by the popular masses.
Глава 10. Совершенствование политической системы социалистического общества в 50-х годах
The improvement of the political system of socialist society in the 1950s. Sections: the XIX Congress of the CPSU; the strengthening and development of Leninist norms of party and state life, the XX Congress of the CPSU — the July (1953) Plenum of the CC of the CPSU, the XX Congress, the XX Congress on the international situation and the prospects of world development, on the tasks of internal development of the country, on intra-party tasks, the growth of the ranks of the CPSU, the further strengthening of party organisations and the extension of their activity; the further development of the Soviet state — the composition of representative organs, the extension of the legislative activity of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR and the Supreme Soviets of the union republics, the extension of the rights of the union republics, the improvement of the activity of the local Soviets, the improvement of the state apparatus, the strengthening of socialist legality, the further strengthening of the defence capacity of the country; the raising of the role of the trade unions and the Komsomol in the development of socialist society.
Глава 11. Индустриальное развитие СССР в 50-х годах
The industrial development of the USSR in the 1950s. Sections: the policy of the Communist Party and the Soviet state in industry — the features and tasks of the new stage, the course toward the acceleration of technical progress, the change of the organisational forms of the administration of industry, the improvement of the system of norming and payment of labour; the change in the composition of industrial cadres, the new labour upsurge of industrial workers — the quantitative and qualitative growth of industrial cadres, the new upsurge of socialist emulation and technical creativity of the masses, the birth of the movement for a communist attitude to labour; the successes in the development of industry and transport — the unfolding of capital construction, the successes in the development of heavy industry, the expansion of the production of consumer goods, transport and communications on the rise.
Глава 12. Подъем сельского хозяйства в 50-х годах
The upsurge of agriculture in the 1950s. Sections: measures of the Communist Party and the Soviet government for the further development of agriculture — the programme of the upsurge of agriculture, the improvement of economic relations between the state and the kolkhozes, the strengthening of the material-technical base of agriculture, the improvement of the guidance of agriculture, the development of the virgin and fallow lands; the upsurge of agricultural production — the growth of the productive activity of the agricultural workers, the results of the struggle for the upsurge of agriculture, the reorganisation of the MTS (machine-tractor stations), the raising of the level of socialisation of agricultural production.
Глава 13. Рост материального благосостояния населения СССР
The growth of the material well-being of the population of the USSR. Sections: the increase of the real incomes of the working people and the expansion of popular consumption — the increase of the incomes of the working people, the reduction of taxation, the cessation of the annual issue of mass state loans, the growth of payments and benefits from the social consumption funds, the improvement of the pension security of the working people, the regulation of prices for consumer goods, the expansion of popular consumption; the improvement of the housing and cultural-domestic conditions of the working people — the growth of housing construction, the improvement of populated places, the improvement of trade and cultural-domestic service of the population, changes in everyday life; the protection of the health of the working people — medical service of the population, the successes of Soviet medicine, the achievements of Soviet sport.
Глава 14. Развитие науки и культуры в 50-х годах
The development of science and culture in the 1950s. Sections: the development of Soviet science — the organisation of scientific work, the achievements of Soviet scientific thought; the development of public education and the training of specialists — the development of the general-education school, the training of specialists; political-educational work — the growth of the network of cultural-educational institutions and the extension of their activity, the press, radio and television; literature and art — the creative upsurge among the artistic intelligentsia, the development of literature, Soviet art.
Глава 15. Итоги развития СССР к началу 60-х годов
The results of the development of the USSR by the beginning of the 1960s. Sections: the strengthening and extension of the material-technical base of socialism — the powerful upsurge of industry, the development of agriculture, the successful competition with capitalism, the rise of the standard of living of the people; the improvement of the social-economic and class structure of Soviet society — the development and convergence of the forms of socialist property, the change in the social structure of Soviet society, the leading class, social changes in the Soviet peasantry, changes in the composition of the intelligentsia; the flourishing and convergence of the socialist nations — the acceleration of the rates of development of the national republics, the steady convergence of the socialist nations; the Soviet country at a new frontier — the XXI Congress of the CPSU, the XXII Congress of the CPSU and the Programme for the building of communism in the USSR, the growing-over of the state of the dictatorship of the proletariat into the all-people’s socialist state.
Приложения (Appendices)
Appendices. Библиография (bibliography) — the documentary and historiographic base of the volume, including the works of V. I. Lenin, party and state documents, and the wider scholarly literature; Список иллюстраций и карт (list of illustrations and maps) — the plates and maps reproduced in the volume (photographs of industrial and cultural figures, maps of industrial construction, the development of the virgin lands, the administrative division of the USSR in 1946, and others).

sources/istoriya-vneshney-politiki-sssr-.title: История внешней политики СССР 1917–1980, Том второй (1945–1980 гг.) (1981)
sources/istoriya-vneshney-politiki-sssr-.content:
История внешней политики СССР 1917–1980, Том второй (1945–1980 гг.)
А. А. Громыко, Б. Н. Пономарев (ред.) — История внешней политики СССР 1917–1980. В двух томах. Том второй (1945–1980 гг.) (History of the Foreign Policy of the USSR 1917–1980, in two volumes, Volume Two 1945–1980). Fourth edition, revised and supplemented, Издательство «Наука», Москва, 1981. The Institute of History of the USSR, Academy of Sciences of the USSR. The second volume of the official Soviet history of Soviet foreign policy, covering the postwar years through the close of the 1970s.





























EditorsА. А. Громыко (A. A. Gromyko, Minister of Foreign Affairs) and Б. Н. Пономарев (B. N. Ponomarev); second-volume authors А. Л. Адамишин, А. М. Александров, А. И. Блатов, А. В. Горев, В. Ф. Грубяков, И. Н. Земсков, В. Л. Исраэлян, М. С. Капица, И. К. Кобляков, Л. Н. Кутаков, А. А. Рощин, Ш. П. Санакоев, С. Л. Тихвинский, В. М. ФалинEditionFourth, revised and supplemented, 1981 (Наука, Москва); print run 50,000; signed to press 2 November 1980; price 3 r. 70 k.StructureTitle page + 19 chapters (XIV–XXXII) + Заключение (Conclusion) + Хронологическая таблица (chronological table) + Установление и восстановление дипломатических отношений СССР + Библиография; 596-page scan (~756 printed pages); 41,424 lines of OCR textPeriod1945–1980: from the end of the Second World War and the postwar settlement through the adoption of the 1977 Constitution and the implementation of the foreign-policy programme of the XXV Party Congress (1976–1980)NoteThe volume continues the numbering of the first volume (1917–1945) from Chapter XIV; it is dedicated to the achievement of a just postwar settlement, the deepening of Soviet relations with the socialist states, mutually advantageous relations with the capitalist states, and aid to peoples fighting for independence
Contents. The second volume of the official Soviet history of foreign policy, continuing the narrative of the first (1917–1945) from the end of the Second World War. It opens with the general international situation and the position of the USSR after the war (XIV), the peace settlement with the former allies of Germany (XV), and the formation of the world socialist system and the new type of international relations (XVI). It then treats the German question in the first postwar years 1945–1949 (XVII), the Soviet struggle for disarmament 1946–1952 (XVIII), the peaceful settlement in the Far East and the occupation of Japan (XIX), the struggle for peace and international cooperation against imperialist policy and the creation of military blocs 1946–1952 (XX), Soviet opposition to imperialist aggression in the Far East and the Korean War (XXI), and the German question after the establishment of the two German states 1949–1955 (XXII). The volume then covers the end of the Korean and Indochinese wars and the easing of tension 1951–1956 (XXIII), disarmament after the creation of the thermonuclear bomb 1953–1958 (XXIV), the Near East crisis and the Hungarian events 1956–1957 (XXV), Soviet aid to the peoples of Asia and Africa in their struggle for independence 1957–1964 (XXVI), the struggle for a German peace settlement and Soviet relations with the GDR 1955–1964 (XXVII), the USSR and the socialist commonwealth 1957–1971 (XXVIII), and new disarmament initiatives 1959–1971 (XXIX). It closes with the struggle against imperialist aggression and Soviet relations with the developing and capitalist countries 1964–1971 (XXX), the implementation of the foreign-policy decisions of the XXIV Party Congress and the Peace Programme in action 1971–1975 (XXXI), and the implementation of the programme for peace and international cooperation adopted by the XXV Party Congress 1976–1980 (XXXII), followed by a conclusion, a chronological table, a list of the establishment and restoration of Soviet diplomatic relations, and a bibliography.
Character of the source. The official Soviet account of the foreign policy of the USSR in the postwar decades, produced under the editorship of the Soviet Foreign Minister (Громыко) and the head of the Central Committee’s international department (Пономарев) and issued by the Institute of History of the USSR of the Academy of Sciences. It presents Soviet foreign policy in the standard terms of the Soviet historiography of the Brezhnev era — as a consistent struggle for peace, disarmament, national liberation and détente against the “imperialist” politics of the United States and its allies, the North Atlantic bloc and the “aggressive circles” of the Western powers. It is a companion in this folder to the История КПСС (1982) and История СССР, Том 11 (1980), with whose periodisation and viewpoint it is consistent.
Quality. Good. Extracted from the supplied PDF (596-page scan) via the embedded text layer; Cyrillic text clean with continuous prose; the table of contents read from the end-of-volume оглавление (Chapter XIV–XXXII + Заключение). Minor page-boundary artefacts and line-wrapping of table-of-contents entries noted during extraction.

Глава XIV (Chapter XIV) — Общая международная обстановка и международное положение СССР после окончания второй мировой войны
The general international situation and the international position of the USSR after the end of the Second World War: the strengthening of Soviet power and international position, the detachment of a number of European and Asian states from the capitalist system and the establishment of the people’s-democratic order in them, the rise of the national-liberation movement in Asia and North Africa, the beginning of the disintegration of the colonial system, and the weakening of the positions of imperialism.
Глава XV (Chapter XV) — Вопросы мирного урегулирования с бывшими союзниками Германии
Questions of the peaceful settlement with the former allies of Germany: the Soviet struggle for the principles of a democratic peace, the Soviet defence of the sovereignty of the vanquished states, the political and territorial provisions of the peace treaties, the economic articles and Soviet defence of the economic independence of Italy, Romania, Bulgaria, Hungary and Finland, and the question of reparations.
Глава XVI (Chapter XVI) — Образование мировой социалистической системы и возникновение международных отношений нового типа
The formation of the world socialist system and the emergence of a new type of international relations: the victory of people’s democracy in the countries of Central and South-Eastern Europe, the development of cooperation and mutual assistance between the USSR and the people’s-democratic states, economic cooperation and the creation of the Council of Economic Mutual Assistance (СЭВ / Comecon).
Глава XVII (Chapter XVII) — Внешняя политика СССР и германский вопрос в первые послевоенные годы (1945—1949 гг.)
Soviet foreign policy and the German question in the first postwar years (1945–1949): the democratic transformations in East Germany, the forgetfulness of the lessons of history in the western zones of occupation, and the collision of the two lines on the question of the unity of Germany.
Глава XVIII (Chapter XVIII) — Борьба СССР за разоружение (1946—1952 гг.)
The Soviet struggle for disarmament (1946–1952): the USSR and the question of prohibiting the atomic weapon, and the struggle for the reduction of conventional armaments and armed forces.
Глава XIX (Chapter XIX) — СССР и вопросы мирного урегулирования на Дальнем Востоке
The USSR and the questions of a peaceful settlement in the Far East: the defeat of Japan and the problems of peaceful settlement, the establishment of American control over Japan, the decisions of the Moscow conference of the foreign ministers on Japan, the struggle for the democratisation and demilitarisation of Japan, the problem of a peace treaty with Japan, the USSR and the San Francisco Conference.
Глава XX (Chapter XX) — Борьба СССР за мир и международное сотрудничество против империалистической политики подавления суверенитета государств и создания военных блоков (1946—1952 гг.)
The struggle of the USSR for peace and international cooperation against the imperialist policy of suppressing the sovereignty of states and creating military blocs (1946–1952): the two lines in international politics, the USSR and the Truman Doctrine, the exposure of the imperialist essence of the Marshall Plan, and the USSR against the imperialist policy of military blocs.
Глава XXI (Chapter XXI) — Советский Союз в борьбе против империалистической агрессии на Дальнем Востоке
The Soviet Union in the struggle against imperialist aggression in the Far East: the USSR against the American policy of dividing Korea and Soviet aid to the Korean people, the preparation and unleashing of the war in Korea, and the struggle for the ending of American intervention in Korea.
Глава XXII (Chapter XXII) — Германский вопрос после образования двух германских государств (1949—1955 гг.)
The German question after the formation of the two German states (1949–1955): two German states and two opposed policies, the Soviet struggle against the plans to arm the FRG and for the fulfilment of the Western powers’ obligations under the alliance agreements, the Soviet plan for a peaceful settlement with Germany, the development of friendly equal relations between the USSR and the GDR, the Berlin conference of the four foreign ministers, the struggle against the inclusion of the FRG in the North Atlantic bloc and the conclusion of the Warsaw Treaty, the German question at the Geneva conferences (1955), the establishment of diplomatic relations between the USSR and the FRG, and the treaty on relations between the USSR and the GDR.
Глава XXIII (Chapter XXIII) — Борьба Советского правительства за прекращение войны в Корее и Вьетнаме, за общее ослабление международной напряженности (1951—1956 гг.)
The struggle of the Soviet government for the ending of the war in Korea and Vietnam and for the general easing of international tension (1951–1956): the end of the Korean War, the Berlin conference of the four foreign ministers, the Geneva conference of 1954 on Korea and Indochina, the USSR and the conclusion of the State Treaty with Austria, the development of good-neighbourly relations with Finland, the Geneva summit, the Geneva conference of the four foreign ministers (1955), the establishment of diplomatic relations with Japan, the further strengthening of fraternal friendship between the USSR and the socialist states, and Soviet support for the peoples’ struggle to win and consolidate their independence.
Глава XXIV (Chapter XXIV) — Советский Союз и проблема разоружения после создания термоядерной бомбы (1953-1958 гг.)
The Soviet Union and the problem of disarmament after the creation of the thermonuclear bomb (1953–1958).
Глава XXV (Chapter XXV) — СССР в борьбе против агрессии на Ближнем Востоке и происков империалистической реакции в Венгрии (1956—1957 гг.)
The USSR in the struggle against aggression in the Near East and the intrigues of imperialist reaction in Hungary (1956–1957): Soviet support for the Arab peoples and the ending of the aggression of England, France and Israel against Egypt, the counter-revolutionary revolt in Hungary, and Soviet opposition to imperialist policy in the Near and Middle East after the Suez crisis.
Глава XXVI (Chapter XXVI) — Помощь Советского Союза народам Азии и Африки в борьбе за независимость (1957—1964 гг.)
Soviet aid to the peoples of Asia and Africa in their struggle for independence (1957–1964): Soviet assistance in the liquidation of colonialism, aid in repelling imperialist aggression against the Arab countries, support for Indonesia, the Geneva conference on Laos, the events in the Congo and the Soviet position, the USSR and the independence of Cyprus, and the development of political ties and Soviet economic aid to the young states of Asia and Africa.
Глава XXVII (Chapter XXVII) — Борьба СССР за германское мирное урегулирование. Развитие дружбы и сотрудничества между СССР и ГДР (1955—1964 гг.)
The struggle of the USSR for a German peace settlement and the development of friendship and cooperation between the USSR and the GDR (1955–1964): the negotiations on a German peace settlement, the protective measures adopted by the GDR government on the borders with West Berlin and the Soviet-American exchange of views, and the further strengthening of fraternal relations and the conclusion of the treaty of friendship, mutual assistance and cooperation between the USSR and the GDR.
Глава XXVIII (Chapter XXVIII) — СССР и страны социалистического содружества (1957—1971 гг.)
The USSR and the countries of the socialist commonwealth (1957–1971): the further development of economic cooperation with the socialist states, Soviet activity in strengthening the solidarity of the socialist countries, the Soviet Union and revolutionary Cuba, and the struggle of the USSR and the other Warsaw Treaty countries for a solution to the problem of European security.
Глава XXIX (Chapter XXIX) — Новые инициативы СССР в борьбе за разоружение (1959—1971 гг.)
New Soviet initiatives in the struggle for disarmament (1959–1971): the proposal for general and complete disarmament at the XIV session of the UN General Assembly, the Committee of Ten on disarmament and the disruption of its work by the Western powers, the Soviet disarmament proposals of 2 June 1960, disarmament at the XV and XVI sessions of the General Assembly, the struggle for general and complete disarmament in the Eighteen-Nation Committee and at the XVII session, the struggle for the ending of atomic and hydrogen weapon tests (1959–1962), the conclusion of the Moscow treaty prohibiting nuclear weapon tests, the struggle against the nuclear arming of the FRG, the conclusion of the non-proliferation treaty, and Soviet efforts for partial disarmament measures.
Глава XXX (Chapter XXX) — Борьба СССР против империалистической агрессии. Отношения СССР с развивающимися странами и капиталистическими государствами (1964—1971 гг.)
The struggle of the USSR against imperialist aggression and its relations with the developing countries and the capitalist states (1964–1971): the American aggression in Indochina and Soviet support for Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia, support for the Arab countries in repelling Israeli aggression and the struggle to liquidate the centre of war in the Near East, Soviet relations with the countries of Asia, Africa and Latin America, relations with the capitalist states, and the questions of European security in relations with the capitalist countries.
Глава XXXI (Chapter XXXI) — Борьба Советского Союза за осуществление внешнеполитических решений XXIV съезда КПСС. Программа мира в действии (1971—1975 гг.)
The struggle of the Soviet Union for the implementation of the foreign-policy decisions of the XXIV Congress of the CPSU and the Peace Programme in action (1971–1975): the Soviet Peace Programme, the further strengthening of the unity of the fraternal socialist states, the USSR and the capitalist states and the new successes of the policy of peaceful coexistence, the Conference on Security and Cooperation in Europe, the struggle for disarmament, the Soviet Union and the developing countries, and the USSR and questions of security in Asia.
Глава XXXII (Chapter XXXII) — Осуществление программы дальнейшей борьбы за мир и международное сотрудничество, за свободу и независимость народов, принятой XXV съездом КПСС (1976—1980 гг.)
The implementation of the programme for the further struggle for peace and international cooperation, for the freedom and independence of peoples, adopted by the XXV Congress of the CPSU (1976–1980): the consolidation in the Constitution of the USSR of the basic principles of Leninist foreign policy, the further strengthening of the positions of world socialism, Soviet cooperation with the socialist states, cooperation within the Comecon system, the struggle for peace, disarmament, international security and détente, Soviet-Chinese relations, relations with the capitalist states, the strengthening of cooperation with the countries freed from colonial and semi-colonial dependence, relations with the countries of Africa, the struggle for a just settlement in the Near East, relations with the Arab countries and the situation in the Middle East, relations with the countries of South and South-East Asia, relations with the countries of Latin America, and the Soviet Union and the non-aligned movement.
Заключение (Conclusion)
A general conclusion on the character and results of Soviet foreign policy over the period covered by the volume, followed by a Хронологическая таблица (chronological table), a list of the establishment and restoration of Soviet diplomatic relations (Установление и восстановление дипломатических отношений СССР), and a Библиография (bibliography).

sources/kowalczuk-die-uebernahme-wie-ost.title: Ilko-Sascha Kowalczuk — Die Übernahme: Wie Ostdeutschland Teil der Bundesrepublik wurde
sources/kowalczuk-die-uebernahme-wie-ost.content:
Ilko-Sascha Kowalczuk — Die Übernahme: Wie Ostdeutschland Teil der Bundesrepublik wurde
Full bibliographic citation — Ilko-Sascha Kowalczuk, Die Übernahme: Wie Ostdeutschland Teil der Bundesrepublik wurde, Verlag C.H. Beck, München, 2019. ISBN 978-3-406-74020-6 (Print) / 978-3-406-74021-3 (E-Book). First published August 2019, on the thirtieth anniversary of the fall of the Berlin Wall. German text; extracted plain text of 8,033 lines.





























AuthorIlko-Sascha Kowalczuk — German historian (born 1967 in East Berlin); among the leading historians of the GDR; author of the standard work Endspiel. Die Revolution von 1989 in der DDR (C.H. Beck, 2009, several editions) and numerous further books on GDR historyEditionVerlag C.H. Beck, München, first published August 2019; ISBN 978-3-406-74020-6 (Print) / 978-3-406-74021-3 (E-Book); published for the thirtieth anniversary of the fall of the WallStructurePersonal opening (Zwischen Aufbruch und Abbruch) + essay proper + twenty-two topical chapters + closing chapter + Danksagung, Anmerkungen, Literaturhinweise, Personenregister; extracted plain text of 8,033 linesPeriod1989/90 to the present — the transformation of East Germany from the fall of the Wall through reunification and the three decades since, and how that past shapes the eastern German presentNoteAn avowed “essay” (in the literal sense of a Versuch, an attempt) written to mark the thirtieth anniversary of 1989: a pointed, opinionated reflection on how the GDR was “taken over” by West Germany and what the social, economic, political and cultural consequences of that takeover have been for eastern Germany. Kowalczuk, himself an East German who served in the 1990s as a member of the Enquete-Kommission of the German Bundestag on the SED dictatorship, sets out to explain “how our present has become historical” — placing hard facts beside personal experience, and pushing deliberately provocative theses about the successes and failures of the transformation (the German subtitle of the book’s publisher advertising calls it “the political book of the hour”). It is as much a critical history of the transformation as a contribution to contemporary debate about democracy, populism and extremism in eastern Germany
Content Summary
Zwischen Aufbruch und Abbruch (opening). Kowalczuk opens with intimate personal and family vignettes that frame the whole essay. The chapter introduces the theme of East German hopes and their frustration through individual stories: “Dieter,” his wife’s father, an East German building-firm director who greeted the fall of the Wall with renewed energy but saw his business collapse under the burden of “Altschulden” (inherited debts) and the privatisation regime of the Treuhand, ending bankrupt, privately liable and dying of cancer on the day he was summoned to court; and Kowalczuk’s own father, an SED member from conviction, a financial economist, born into an ethnically-German family expelled from Bohemia in 1946. Through these histories Kowalczuk sets up his central theme: the coexistence in East German biographies of Anpassung and Selbstbehauptung (adaptation and self-assertion), of Mitmachen and Widerspruch (complicity and dissent), of Überzeugung and Verrat (conviction and betrayal) — often within a single person.
Der Essay. The framing introduction. Kowalczuk explains that he writes to show “how our present has become historical,” drawing on three decades of scholarly work on the history and consequences of communism in Germany and Europe. He situates the essay in a moment when Western conceptions of democracy and freedom have come under pressure from within as well as without. He insists the essay is not about the infinite details of history but about the great lines and questions that impose themselves if we want to understand the present — hence “a look back.” He warns about the limits of statistics and opinion polls (which “sharpen and invent realities”), and announces that he will deliberately sharpen and provoke in order to make problems visible.
Der letzte Republikgeburtstag. The last GDR republic anniversary — the fortieth anniversary of the founding of the GDR on 7 October 1989 — as the moment when the regime’s terminal crisis became unmistakable. Kowalczuk describes the atmosphere in East Berlin on that day, contrasting the regime’s anniversary celebrations with the reality of a collapsing state; Chilean emigrants in the GDR are quoted comparing the tension to the eve of the Chilean coup.
Unmittelbare Folgen des Mauerfalls. The immediate consequences of the fall of the Wall on 9 November 1989: the unprecedented mass movement of people, the opening of the border, and the sudden, disorienting entry of West German reality into the East.
Vom Runden Tisch zu freien Wahlen. From the Central Round Table to free elections. Kowalczuk traces the negotiated transition of power in the GDR — the emergence of the “Zentraler Runder Tisch” from December 1989, where government and opposition sat together, the dissolution of the SED’s monopoly, and the road to the first free Volkskammer election of 18 March 1990.
Neue Erfahrung: Arbeitslosigkeit. The new experience of unemployment. The collapse of the GDR economy threw a third of East German employment onto the streets: the GDR had 9.7 million employed in 1989 but only 6.2 million by the end of 1993. Kowalczuk analyses the labour-market catastrophe, the role of the Treuhand in closing plants, the DGB’s failings in the East, and the Reichsbahn strike as a signal of the new conflicts.
Der Beitritt: alternativlos? “The accession: was there no alternative?” A critical examination of the process by which the GDR acceded to the Federal Republic under Article 23 rather than a constitution-drafting path under Article 146 of the Basic Law. Kowalczuk recounts the cool reception of the Modrow government in Bonn in February 1990, the “deutsch-deutsche Wahlkampf” of Kohl’s election campaign, and the argument that the accession route was presented as “alternativlos” (without alternative) — a claim he interrogates.
Was wäre wenn …? “What if …?” A counterfactual reflection on whether the transformation could have taken a different, less one-sided form — what a genuinely negotiated unity, or a longer transition, might have looked like.
In was für einer Verfassung? “In what kind of constitution?” The constitutional question of German unity: the failure to give the new Germany a new constitution and the adoption instead of the Basic Law, and what that choice meant for eastern Germans.
Wer sind Ostdeutsche? “Who are the East Germans?” A chapter on the very definition of “East German” — the historical space that no longer exists since 1945, the five new Länder (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Brandenburg, Sachsen-Anhalt, Thüringen, Sachsen) of about 12.6 million inhabitants on roughly 108,000 square kilometres, and the special case of Berlin with its 3.6 million inhabitants.
Ostdeutsche als «Andere». East Germans as “the others.” Kowalczuk analyses how East Germans were constructed as a distinct, exotic, often deficient “other” in the unified republic, and the asymmetry of mutual perception between East and West.
Die Forderung: «Anpassung» and Die Angepassten. The demand for “adaptation” and “the adapted.” On the one-sided expectation that East Germans adapt to Western norms, institutions and habits after 1990, and the figure of the “Angepasste” — the accommodating East German.
Die Hauptstadtdebatte. The Berlin capital debate — the 1991 Bundestag decision to make Berlin (not Bonn) the seat of government and parliament, and what it signified.
Stagnation. Economic stagnation and only a slight recovery, driven above all by the booming construction sector in the East.
Die Treuhand. The Treuhandanstalt — the most important shaper of the first half of the 1990s. Kowalczuk analyses how the Treuhand privatised, liquidated or “gesundgeschrumpft” (shrunk to health) some 8,000 Volkseigene Betriebe (people’s enterprises), and the social devastation this caused.
Die Eigentumsfrage. The property question: the restitution of property expropriated under the GDR and its enormous administrative and social costs (“Rückgabe vor Entschädigung”).
Die Landwirtschaft. Agriculture: the GDR’s collectivised agriculture (large LPG cooperatives) confronted with Western agricultural policy, and the collapse of East German farming.
Der ökonomische Kollaps als Kulturkampf. The economic collapse as a cultural struggle — Kowalczuk’s argument that the economic transformation was experienced and fought out by East Germans also as an assault on their ways of life and self-respect.
Das Unverständnis für Ostdeutschland. The West’s failure to understand East Germany.
Das Beschäftigungsproblem. The employment problem in the East across the decades since 1990.
Die kulturelle Ausgrenzung. Cultural exclusion — the marginalisation of East German voices, experiences and cultural producers in the unified republic.
Mobilität als Problem. Mobility as a problem — the permanent East-West migration of the young and skilled and its demographic consequences.
Rentenprobleme. Pension problems — the long-running and politically explosive grievance over East German pension entitlements.
Gewinnerinnen oder Verliererinnen? Winners or losers? Kowalczuk weighs who profited and who lost from the transformation, insisting the answers are not as simple as the clichés suggest.
Neue Benachteiligungen. New disadvantages — the forms of structural disadvantage East Germans continued to face.
Der Elitenaustausch an den Universitäten. The elite exchange at the universities — how the East German academic and intellectual elite was replaced after 1990, and the consequences of that break.
Ost-Eliten im vereinigten Deutschland. East German elites in united Germany — the small number of East Germans in leading positions of the economy, politics, media and culture, and the resulting “Kolonialisierung” debates.
Irgendwie alle! “Somehow everyone!” On the East-West institutional fusions and their bitter, often farcical conflicts — the “war of the arts” over the fusion of the East and West Berlin Academies of the Arts, where Heiner Müller, last president of the East Academy, warned in July 1990 that what was happening was “a process of conquest, of subjugation, not of unification,” invoking Cortés and the Catholic churches built on the Aztec temples of Mexico.
Gesellschaftspolitische Dimensionen der Aufarbeitung. The socio-political dimensions of coming to terms with the past — the Stasi files, the Gauck authority, and the social conflicts of “Aufarbeitung” (the official reckoning with the SED dictatorship).
Demokratie ohne Demokraten. “Democracy without democrats.” One of the essay’s central chapters: Kowalczuk notes that 87.5 per cent of the GDR population in 1989 had no personal experience of a functioning democratic state (only the generation born 1923 or earlier had known Weimar), that the civic democracy had been systematically vilified under both the Nazi dictatorship and the GDR, and that this legacy made eastern Germany a “democracy without democrats” — a society that inherited democratic institutions without democratic habit.
Antisemitismus, Illiberale Einstellungen, Nationalismus, Rassismus. Four successive chapters on eastern German attitudes: antisemitism, illiberal attitudes, nationalism and racism — measured against polling data and the rise of right-wing populism.
Medien in Ostdeutschland. The media landscape in eastern Germany — the takeover of the East German media by Western companies, the collapse of the GDR’s newspapers, and the distinctive eastern media market.
Wahlen im Osten. Elections in the East: persistently lower turnout than the federal average since the first all-German election of 2 December 1990 (swinging between 82.2 per cent in 1998 and 70.8 per cent in 2009), the East-West split in Bundestag results, and the success of right-wing populists and extremists in the East.
Zwischen 1989: Hoffnungslosigkeit und 1990: Hoffnungen. The closing chapter — “Between 1989: hopelessness and 1990: hopes.” Kowalczuk contrasts the East Germans’ hopelessness as they entered 1989 (when even the hope of change was rare and a larger minority fled, risking their lives) with the boundless hope with which they entered 1990 and reunification. He catalogues the groups that were later disappointed — the victims of the communists (whom the Rechtsstaat did not properly honour or compensate), the loyal SED system-goers (who felt disadvantaged and humiliated), the workers who lost their jobs, the scientists whose knowledge was no longer needed, the farmers whose agriculture got by without them, the civil-rights activists whose counsel the citizens no longer valued. He ends by sketching “Zukunftsvisionen für Ostdeutschland” (future visions for East Germany) in the early 1990s, and reflects on the fragmenting, globalising world and the temptation of new totalitarian claims.
Anhang. Danksagung (acknowledgements); Anmerkungen (notes, pp. 1–238 in this EPUB by chapter); Literaturhinweise (a selective bibliography indicating the breadth of the research); Personenregister (index of persons).
